narrativeBlocks.title: An unannounced arrival
narrativeBlocks.body: Theseus walks into Athens a hero — but tells no one who he is. At his father's court sits Medea, the sorceress who fled Corinth, living with the ageing King Aegeus on her promise to give him an heir by her arts.

narrativeBlocks.title: Medea sees through him
narrativeBlocks.body: Medea recognizes the stranger before anyone else does — and understands at once that a true son of Aegeus ends her influence and her children's claim. She persuades the suspicious old king that the newcomer is a spy, and offers to handle it herself: a cup of poison at dinner.

narrativeBlocks.title: The sword on the table
narrativeBlocks.body: The meat is served. Theseus draws his sword as if to carve — the sword he pulled from under the rock. Aegeus recognizes the token instantly, strikes the poisoned cup to the floor, and embraces his son before the whole court.

narrativeBlocks.title: A public heir
narrativeBlocks.body: Aegeus gathers the citizens and publicly owns Theseus as his son. Medea flees Athens — the same sorceress Jason will face across the sea, in a story you will meet later this week.

narrativeBlocks.title: Why the token matters
narrativeBlocks.body: Greek recognition scenes turn on objects — a sword, a scar, a bed. The tokens Aegeus hid at Troezen do not just prove bloodline; they complete the journey Theseus chose the hard way.

quiz.prompt: How does Aegeus discover the stranger is his son?

choices.text: Theseus draws the hidden sword at dinner, and Aegeus recognizes the token he left under the rock
Medea reveals Theseus's identity out of remorse
A birthmark is spotted by the palace servants

quiz.explanation: At dinner Theseus draws his sword 'as if he designed to cut with it'; Aegeus recognizes the token and knocks the poisoned cup away.

quiz.prompt: Why did Medea want Theseus poisoned?

choices.text: A true son of Aegeus would end her influence at court and her children's claim to inherit
She was loyal to King Minos
Aegeus ordered her to test him

quiz.explanation: Medea lived at Aegeus's court promising him an heir; a real son arriving meant she lost everything, so she framed Theseus as a spy and poisoned his cup.
